newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to extend offset deal with Saab.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to extend offset deal with Saab.

text.p: Hungary will extend on Wednesday an industrial agreement signed with Sweden's plane maker Saab AB, the ministry of industry and trade (IKIM) said on Monday.
"The new protocol sets the rules for certain possible offset deals," an IKIM official told Reuters.

Saab offered to offset the price of its Gripen planes with investments and export deals should Hungary opt for the Swedish fighter in a procurement deal to replace part of its ageing MiG fighter fleet.
The original tender, which was due out last year, was postponed until at least the start of accession talks with NATO.
The offset agreement with Saab was signed in September 1995 and expired on December 31, 1996.
Hungary -- depending on the timescale of NATO membership -- is looking to buy some 30 fighters.

Leading bidders in the race for the contract are Lockheed Martin Corp with its F16, either new or used, Saab, McDonnell Douglas Corp -Northrop Grumman Corp with its F-18 and Dassault Aviation which is offering the Mirage 2000-5.
McDonnell Douglas also signed last December an industrial offset deal with Hungary.
The IKIM official said the ministry is conducting talks with other bidders about offset agreements, but did not elaborate.
Hungary has a squadron of 28 MiG-29s that would be operational well into the next century, but its older Soviet-made MiG-21, MiG-23 and Su-22 airplanes need replacement.
